description.plain:
CARD 1

Business Questions & Audience

Dashboard overview and business context

Dashboard Overview

Dashboard Name: O2C Receivables Intelligence

Purpose: Provide connected visibility across receivables, collections, credit exposure and Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), linking the sales order, delivery, billing and cash-collection lifecycle in one analytical experience.

Business Problem

The scenario describes a manufacturing business where receivables and order-book reporting are reviewed in separate extracts. DSO, overdue ageing and dispute exposure are calculated manually, while open orders, blocked orders, deliveries and financial receivables remain disconnected. This delays dispute discovery, makes credit intervention reactive and limits end-to-end cycle-time visibility.

Target Audience

Persona — Purpose

Executive Leadership / CFO — Monitor revenue, open receivables, DSO, credit utilisation, revenue at risk and regional risk concentration.

Credit Control / FI-AR — Identify overdue customers, ageing exposure, credit-limit utilisation, blocked accounts and dunning priorities.

Sales Leadership — Understand customer exposure, order and billing status, customer-group risk and revenue potentially affected by credit blocks.

Collections Team — Prioritise customers using overdue amount, expected collection date, payment behaviour and historical payment delay.

Finance / O2C Analysts — Reconcile AR balances, investigate ageing and explain order-to-cash cycle-time leakage.

Plant / Company-Code Controllers — Review entity-specific receivables and credit exposure within assigned company-code access.

Five Key Business Questions

What is my DSO trend by company code and customer group over the last 13 months, and which 10 customers move it most?

What is my ageing waterfall today (current / 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / 90+), and how did it shift versus last month?

Where is order-to-cash cycle time leaking — order-to-delivery, delivery-to-billing or billing-to-collection?

Which customers exceed 80% of credit limit including open orders and deliveries, and what revenue is at risk if blocked?

What cash can I realistically expect to collect in the next 30 days based on due dates and historical payment behaviour?

description.plain:
CARD 5

Drill-Down Story

Executive monitoring → credit investigation → collection and process action

Start with the Executive Overview to locate movement in revenue, open receivables, DSO or regional risk. Move to Credit & Product Performance to identify customers approaching or exceeding their credit limits and the product divisions associated with exposure. Continue to O2C Cycle & Collection Intelligence to isolate cycle-time leakage and prioritise collection action.

Step — Dashboard Perspective — Investigation / Expected Action

1 — Executive Overview — Review Total Open Receivables, DSO, Credit Utilization and Revenue at Risk. Filter by company code, customer, city, AR status and customer group to locate concentration.

2 — Credit & Product Performance — Compare customer credit exposure with credit limit; inspect customers above 80% utilisation, blocked customers, product-division exposure and overdue balances.

3 — O2C Cycle & Collection Intelligence — Compare order-to-delivery, delivery-to-billing and billing-to-collection days. Review payment score, average payment delay and payment terms.

4 — Follow-up / Control — Confirm FI open-item balances, customer credit master values, due dates, filter context and source refresh before taking action.

Expected Business Action

Collections: prioritise high-value overdue items and customers with weak payment behaviour or long historical delays.

Credit control: review customers nearing or exceeding limits; coordinate blocked-customer decisions with Sales and Finance.

Process improvement: investigate whether cycle-time leakage is concentrated in delivery, billing or cash application.

Management: use company-code and regional views to align working-capital actions with the responsible operating entity.

description.plain:
CARD 6

Insights & ROI

Dashboard observations and a defensible business-value framework

Key Dashboard Insights

Area — Dashboard Observation — Evidence / Note

Receivables position — Executive Overview displays ₹9.19 crore Total Open Receivables and DSO of 136 days. — Displayed dashboard values; reconcile against FI open-item balances and trailing-12-month billed revenue.

Credit position — Credit page displays ₹464.20 crore total credit limit and ₹296.24 crore total credit exposure. — Displayed values; customer-level exception aggregation required.

Credit risk — Four blocked customers are displayed; top high-risk customers and customers above 80% utilisation are ranked. — Confirm blocked-customer distinct-count logic and credit exposure calculation.

Ageing — Executive page shows 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 90+ ageing categories. — Dashboard displays ageing distribution; month-over-month comparison data is not supplied in the PDF.

Cycle-time leakage — Billing-to-collection is 108.03 days versus 14.97 days order-to-delivery and 4.06 days delivery-to-billing. — Displayed average intervals; validate timestamp definitions, exclusions and averaging method.

Geographic risk — Map and regional panels show receivables / credit concentration across Americas, Europe and India operations. — Confirm geo mapping, currency normalisation and regional grouping rules.

ROI Documentation Format

Value Area — Before Dashboard — After Dashboard / Measurement

Executive visibility — Static weekly extracts and separate SD/FI reporting; baseline effort not supplied. — Connected SAC overview; measure report preparation time and decision latency.

Receivables & ageing — Manual Excel calculations with differing overdue definitions. — Centralised ageing buckets and open AR measure; measure reconciliation effort and ageing visibility.

Credit intervention — Credit exposure not visible alongside open orders, deliveries and invoices at decision time. — Customer-level exposure and utilisation views; measure blocked-order incidents and overdue exposure.

Collections — Follow-up relies on separate customer/payment information. — Customer-level payment delay, score and expected collection indicators; measure collection effectiveness and cash forecast accuracy.

Process efficiency — End-to-end order, delivery, billing and collection intervals not visible together. — Cycle-time stages are visible; measure stage-level delay reduction and billing-to-collection improvement.

ROI Statement

The delivered dashboard brings receivables, credit risk, customer collection behaviour and O2C cycle-time analysis into a connected SAC experience. The supplied sources do not quantify realised time savings, DSO reduction, cash acceleration, bad-debt reduction or financial ROI. These outcomes must be measured against an agreed baseline after production adoption.
